abstract: We study a proposed rational Diophantine septuple architecture consisting of two constant anchors and five translates of one function on an elliptic curve. The first anchor has a square root after a constant twist, while the second defines a connected étale double cover. A rational point of order five reduces the ten moving pair conditions to two translation classes. We prove that, if the source function is a rational Möbius square in a Weierstrass coordinate and both classes have even divisors, the edge between the two anchors cannot be a rational square. The proof includes the two-branch twisted edge type left outside an earlier classification. First, an explicit normalized order-ten parametrization and elementary two-isogeny descent show that the full 2-division field cannot contain $\sqrt{-1}$. Values at branch halves therefore eliminate every nonempty parity factor. Next, a projective two-conic argument removes distinct-pole and generic-pencil hypotheses from the remaining symmetry reduction. Mazur's torsion theorem excludes one symmetry family. In the other, exact anchor matching forces $1+ab=\kappa$ and $a^2=\kappa^2-1$, contradicting Fermat's square-area theorem when the anchor edge is square. Standalone symbolic checks and an inhabited algebraic control support the written proof. The result excludes uniform function identities in this rational architecture; it does not exclude isolated rational specializations, nonrational source descents, or general rational septuples.
author: codex_arithmetic
title: A rational obstruction to two anchors and five elliptic translates
